points.title: HTML form
points.must: Definition: part of a page made with <form> containing input controls that collect data from the user and send it to a script for processing.
points.model: HTML form = part of a web page (<form> element) containing input controls (text boxes, radio buttons, checkboxes, lists, buttons) that collect data from the user and send it to a script for processing when submitted. The form collects; the script processes.

points.title: Request–response cycle
points.must: The 5 steps: browser requests page → server sends HTML form → user submits, browser sends new HTTP request to action → script reads, validates, processes, outputs HTML → response displayed. Script runs once per request.
points.model: 1) Browser (client) sends HTTP request for the page. 2) Server sends HTML response with the form. 3) User clicks Submit → browser sends a new HTTP request with name=value pairs to the script in action. 4) Script reads → validates → processes (calculate / database) → outputs HTML. 5) Server sends this HTML back as the response; browser shows it. The script runs once per request, top to bottom.

points.title: action and method attributes
points.must: action = address of the script that processes the data (missing → same page); method = how data is sent, get or post (missing → GET). Example opening tag.
points.model: action = the script that receives the data, e.g. action="booking.php" (left out → same page). method = how the data is sent: get or post (left out → GET). Example: <form action="booking.php" method="post">

points.title: GET method and query string
points.must: GET puts data in the URL as a query string: ?name=value&name=value; visible, bookmarkable, length-limited; example URL; use for searches.
points.model: GET: data added to the URL as a query string: ? then name=value pairs separated by &, e.g. search.php?city=Astana&type=dental. Visible in address bar, history and logs; can be bookmarked/shared; limited length. Use for searches/filters that only read data. Read with $_GET["city"].

points.title: POST method and GET vs POST
points.must: POST puts data in the request body: not in URL/history, no size limit, files, not bookmarkable, re-send warning; not encryption (needs HTTPS); use for logins, orders, uploads.
points.model: POST: data in the body of the HTTP request — not shown in URL or history, no practical size limit, can upload files, cannot be bookmarked, browser warns before re-sending. Not encrypted — needs HTTPS. Use for logins, registrations, orders, uploads (requests that change data or are private). Read with $_POST["login"].

points.title: Input controls
points.must: text, number, email, password, radio, checkbox, select, textarea, hidden, submit — what each is for and what it sends.
points.model: text – one line; number – number with min/max; email – checks @; password – shown as dots; radio – choose exactly one of a group; checkbox – tick any number; select/option – drop-down list, sends option value; textarea – several lines; hidden – value not shown but sent (e.g. clinic_id=7); submit – sends the form.

points.title: Radio buttons and checkboxes
points.must: Radio group shares one name, sends only the chosen value; unticked checkbox sends nothing (key missing) → check with isset or ??.
points.model: Radio buttons of one question have the SAME name and different values; only the chosen value is sent (size=M). A checkbox sends its value only if ticked; an unticked checkbox sends nothing at all, so the script must check it with isset() or ??.

points.title: The name attribute
points.must: name = the key under which the value is sent; the script reads it with that key; no name → not sent; must match exactly; id is not sent.
points.model: name attribute = the key under which the control's value is sent; the script reads the value with it: name="quantity" → $_POST["quantity"] (JS: form.elements["quantity"].value). A control without a name is not sent; the key must match exactly (case-sensitive); id is NOT sent.

points.title: Form data is text; HTML5 validation
points.must: All values arrive as strings → convert with (int)/(float)/Number(); required, min, max, maxlength, type=email, pattern give browser checks but can be bypassed.
points.model: All form values arrive as strings ("2", not 2) → convert: (int)$_POST["qty"], (float)…, Number(…) in JS. HTML checks: required (presence), min/max (range), maxlength (length), type="email", pattern="[0-9]{12}" (format). They give instant feedback but can be bypassed, so the server must validate again.

points.title: $_GET and $_POST superglobals
points.must: Built-in associative arrays available everywhere; keys = field names, values = what was entered.
points.model: Superglobal = built-in PHP associative array available everywhere in a script. $_GET holds data sent in the URL (GET), $_POST data sent in the body (POST). Key = name of the control, value = what the user entered: $_POST["qty"].

points.title: isset() and empty()
points.must: isset = key exists and not null (was it sent?); empty = missing or "", "0", 0, null (left blank?); empty("0") trap; ?? default.
points.model: isset($_POST["f"]) – true if the field was sent (not null): form submitted? checkbox ticked? empty($_POST["f"]) – true if missing or "", "0", 0, null → presence check for text boxes. Trap: empty("0") is true. Default value: $extras = $_POST["extras"] ?? [];

points.title: Escaping output with htmlspecialchars()
points.must: User could type HTML/JS that the browser runs (XSS); htmlspecialchars converts < > & " into entities so it is shown as text; validate input, escape output.
points.model: If user text is echoed directly, a user can type <script>…</script> which other browsers run = cross-site scripting (XSS). htmlspecialchars() converts < → <, > → >, & → &, " → ", so the input is displayed as text, not run. Rule: validate input, escape output.

points.title: Steps of a PHP form handler
points.must: Order: check submitted → read by name → convert → validate → process → output escaped; with a short code example.
points.model: 1 check submitted: if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] === "POST") 2 read: $qty = (int)($_POST["qty"] ?? 0); 3 validate: if ($qty < 1 || $qty > MAX_PIZZAS) error 4 process: $total = PRICES[$size] * $qty; 5 output: echo "Thank you, " . htmlspecialchars($customer);

points.title: Server-side vs client-side processing
points.must: PHP on server: trusted, cannot be bypassed, database access, needs a request; JS in browser: instant, can be bypassed, code visible. Rule: browser for convenience, server for security.
points.model: Server-side (PHP): runs after submit, cannot be bypassed, can use the database and secret data, code hidden, needs a page reload → trusted validation, saving, prices. Client-side (JS): runs in the browser, instant feedback, can be switched off/edited, code visible → convenience checks, live totals. Check in the browser for convenience, on the server for security.
